question: If 3 tanθ = 2sqrt 3 sinθ, 0° frac{{cos e{c²}2 theta + {{cot }²}2 theta }}{{{{sin }²} theta + {{tan }²}2 theta }} is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given 3 tanθ = 2√3 sinθ ⇒ 3(sinθ / cosθ) = 2√3 sinθ.

Since 0° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 3 tanθ = 2√3 sinθ

**Formula Used:** tanθ = sinθ / cosθ; cosec 60° = 2/√3; cot 60° = 1/√3; sin 30° = 1/2; tan 60° = √3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e383c522fe45f4a5e2c9acb92385988d9813bb50b7926936b1a0f0a87edbc96.png] 

Step 1: Solve for θ

⇒ 3(sinθ/cosθ) = 2√3 sinθ

⇒ 3/cosθ = 2√3

⇒ cosθ = 3 / 2√3 = (3 × √3) / (2 × 3) = √3 / 2

⇒ θ = cos−¹(√3/2) = 30°

Step 2: Evaluate the expression (cosec² 2θ + cot² 2θ) / (sin² θ + tan² 2θ)

⇒ For θ = 30°, 2θ = 60°

⇒ Numerator = cosec² 60° + cot² 60° = (2/√3)² + (1/√3)² = 4/3 + 1/3 = 5/3

⇒ Denominator = sin² 30° + tan² 60° = (1/2)² + (√3)² = 1/4 + 3 = 13/4

⇒ Final Value = (5/3) / (13/4) = (5/3) × (4/13) = 20/39

**∴ The correct answer is 20/39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Specific Values

Standard values for 30°: sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, tan 30° = 1/√3. For 60°: sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3.

Reciprocal Identities

cosecθ = 1/sinθ, secθ = 1/cosθ, and cotθ = 1/tanθ = cosθ/sinθ.

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.</p
